ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), articles L561-1 to L561-54 and R561-1 et seq.; UBO declaration under articles L561-2-2 and R561-14-1 to R561-14-10; French Commercial Code, articles L123-1 to L123-35 (RCS and Guichet Unique); Law Sapin II 2016-1691 and Law 2018-898 transposing EU AMLD4/AMLD5; TRACFIN enabling provisions under Decree 2018-290; French economic and financial sanctions regime under articles L562-1 to L562-15, incorporating EU and UN consolidated sanctions.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the shareholder/manager's national passport
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of the country of origin (e.g., Chinese Public Security Bureau, French Consulate abroad)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if country not party to the 1961 Convention) followed by certified translation into French by a sworn translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill, tenancy contract or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, landlord, or licensed credit institution in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy, apostille/consular legalization if requested, and French sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for the initial capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original signed letter, legalized or apostilled in line with the bank's jurisdiction, and translated into French if necessary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance/certificate of non-condemnation for the proposed manager (if required by domiciliation agent or bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial authority of the manager's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus French sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized or consular power of attorney for the French formation representative / registered-office agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization) and French sworn translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Draft articles of association (statuts SARL) and signed commercial domiciliation agreement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: French legal counsel / approved domiciliation company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Prepared under French law; no apostille required, but signature legalization applies when executed abroad and notarization is required only for real-property contributions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Apply risk-based customer due diligence under AMLD5/French Monetary and Financial Code: (i) mandatory politically exposed persons (PEP) screening against HATVP and international PEP lists; (ii) screening against U.S. OFAC-SDN, UN Security Council, EU consolidated financial sanctions, and French Direction générale du Trésor national lists; (iii) negative-media and adverse-information checks; (iv) verification of UBO at 25% threshold and all senior managing officials; (v) ongoing transaction monitoring for cash-flow anomalies; (vi) record-keeping for at least 5 years after business relationship ends; (vii) mandatory STR reporting to TRACFIN for any suspected money laundering or terrorist financing.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr) with official name verification performed at INPI's Registre National des Entreprises (RNE); compatibility search via Infogreffe and INPI databases.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A French SARL's dénomination sociale must be written in Latin characters and may be in French or a foreign language; if non-French, a French equivalent/translation may be disclosed and the company cannot use a name that fails to identify the legal form. The RNE/Guichet Unique will transliterate non-Latin names into Latin script using official romanization; all statutory documents, contracts and invoicing must state the legal form and capital.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banque, Établissement de crédit, Société de financement, Financement
Avocat, Notaire, Huissier, Commissaire de justice, Commissaire aux comptes
Bourse, Valeurs mobilières, Conseil en investissements financiers (without license)
Ministère, Préfecture, Mairie, Municipal, National, République (false official suggestion)
Caisse des Dépôts, Banque de France, Sûreté, Police, Gendarmerie
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No separate government name reservation is mandatory for an SARL; a proposed name is checked during Guichet Unique/RNE filing. If the registry or the legal-publication journal (JAL) identifies an identity conflict or prohibited token, the applicant must withdraw and resubmit with a revised name; there is no formal administrative appeal against a non-binding name-proposal refusal. If the RCS registrar rejects the incorporation statement citing name irregularity, the applicant may apply to the competent commercial court (tribunal de commerce) under a simplified contentious procedure, or file a fresh application after correcting the name. For conflicting prior trademarks, opposition/litigation lies before the EUIPO (for EU trade marks) or the French National Institute of Intellectual Property (INPI) under the Code de la propriété intellectuelle.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permitted for an SARL engaged in UI/UX design-as-a-service under Articles L123-11-1 and R123-167 of the French Commercial Code, but it must be operated through a licensed 'domiciliation commerciale' agent located in France. The domiciliation agreement generally cannot exceed 5 consecutive years and must identify a physical registered seat (siège social) in France; the company must keep accounting, corporate and UBO records at that address or at the domiciliation agent's premises. Full 'virtual' operation without any local management presence increases substance risk but is legally viable if the manager declares the seat and exercises control from abroad.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a low-risk digital design-subscription company: approximate 2-4% annual likelihood of spontaneous on-site inspection by the registry, social-security authorities (URSSAF) or tax inspectors, but the probability rises to 10-20% if the entity applies for intra-group services, claims tax advantages, or is selected for a tax audit. Inspections can be unannounced at the registered office under the French tax audit and anti-abuse procedures.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-43 and R.223-1 to R.223-31 concerning the constitution, management and operation of a Société à Responsabilité Limitée; complemented by Articles 1832 and 1835 to 1864 of the French Civil Code (Code civil) on the contract of company.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registre du commerce et des sociétés (RCS), maintained by the Greffe du tribunal de commerce; all filings are submitted through the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI) Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form M0 / Official electronic constitutional filing dossier submitted via the INPI Guichet unique, including the signed articles of association and supporting annexes.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SARL. The articles must fix the capital amount; all shares must be fully subscribed and cash contributions fully paid up before registration. Cash capital must be deposited in a blocked escrow account and released only upon issuance of the Kbis extract.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by unanimous first resolution, that: (1) all share subscriptions set out in the capital table are hereby accepted, the capital is fully issued and the Company is constituted; (2) the registered office is established at the address stated in the articles of association, and the Gérant may record administrative changes in the office; (3) [Name] [Surname] is appointed Gérant of the Company, holding all powers of management and representation conferred by the Code de commerce and the articles; and (4) the Gérant and any authorized agent are empowered to execute, file and pursue the mandatory incorporation formalities with the relevant registries.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Constitutional drafting and adoption of the articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notarial or legal drafting team; final registration authority is the Greffe du tribunal de commerce via the INPI Guichet unique.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts in French and have each founding shareholder sign, either in private writing or before a notary where required. Include the corporate purpose, SARL legal form, registered office, share capital, share distribution, in-kind contribution valuation, duration (maximum 99 years) and appointment of the Gérant. Obtain all signatures on a single version of the deed to avoid contradictory texts.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of association
Capital contribution table and subscription statement
Valid identity document for each shareholder
Declaration of non-conviction for the appointed Gérant
Availability certificate or research memo confirming the corporate name is not already registered on the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry objects to the name, corporate purpose, or statutory wording, amend the articles by supplementary resolution and re-execute the deed; provide certified French translations for any foreign shareholder documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Subscription and full release of share capital through a blocked deposit account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ACPR-licensed French bank or Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; independent contribution auditor for in-kind contributions above the statutory threshold.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the name of the future company and deposit all cash capital. Obtain a bank capital deposit certificate (attestation de consignation). If in-kind contributions are made, obtain a valuation report from a commissaire aux apports when required by the Commercial Code. The funds remain frozen until the RCS registration is completed and the Kbis extract is issued.
required_dossiers: Bank capital deposit certificate
Contribution valuation report, if applicable
Share subscription and paid-up capital statement signed by each shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses to issue the attestation or the contribution valuation is challenged, appoint a replacement bank or contribution auditor and issue a corrected deposit certificate before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal incorporation notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Journal d'annonces légales (JAL) authorized in the territorial department of the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the legal notice text containing the corporate name, legal form, share capital, registered office, corporate purpose, duration and Gérant identity. After publication, obtain the attestation de parution issued by the JAL; this certificate must be included in the final RCS filing dossier.
required_dossiers: Draft text of the legal announcement
Payment receipt for the publication
Original attestation de parution issued by the JAL
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the publication is refused or contains material defects, correct the announcement and arrange a revised publication; ensure the new attestation matches the final articles of association.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation dossier through the INPI single electronic window
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI), Guichet unique des formalités d'entreprises.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the official electronic M0 form and upload all required constitutional documents. The INPI platform routes the dossier to the RCS registrar, DRIEETS and tax authorities. Pay any applicable greffe fees through the platform and retain the electronic acknowledgment of filing.
required_dossiers: Form M0 / statutory declaration of conformity
Signed final version of the articles of association
Acte de nomination of the Gérant
Attestation de parution issued by the authorized JAL
Bank attestation for the deposit of cash capital
Registered-office occupancy document or domiciliation agreement
Declaration of beneficial owner (déclaration de bénéficiaire effectif)
Identity documents and declaration of non-conviction for the Gérant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the file is rejected or marked incomplete, follow the INPI platform instructions within the prescribed period by uploading the requested missing documents; if necessary, submit a formal rectification request to the registry or seek judicial intervention at the competent civil court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Kbis extract and post-registration corporate governance formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; RCS registrar.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon registration, collect the extrait Kbis, verify the SIREN number, APE/NAF code, VAT intra-community number, registered office and legal form. Register the company as an employer with URSSAF/INSEE, open a permanent French business bank account, and establish the statutory corporate books, share register and minutes book.
required_dossiers: Extrait Kbis
BODACC notice of creation
French tax identification number and VAT intra-community number
Share register and corporate books, once established
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains incorrect information or omits an appointed officer, file an application for supplementary registration or rectification with the Greffe; if tax or social identifiers are delayed, contact the local Service des impôts des entreprises and URSSAF directly.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Direction régionale de l'économie, de l'emploi, du travail et des solidarités (DRIEETS) for workplace and occupational safety oversight; Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL) for environmental inspection; no separate industrial manufacturing licensing board applies to ISIC 7410.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No standalone design-activity operating permit; the applicable operating authorization is the RCS registration combined, where applicable, with an ERP compliance certificate (attestation ERP) for offices open to the public and employer establishment registration under the Labor Code.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction régionale de l'environnement, de l'aménagement et du logement (DREAL), French Ministry for the Ecological Transition and Territorial Cohesion.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA for ordinary UI/UX design and subscription offices; classified installation registration may apply only if non-office industrial prototype activities are introduced.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge regulations; VOC-emitting activities such as printing or prototype finishing must comply with EU Directive 2004/42/EC solvent emission limits; all electrical and electronic equipment waste must be transferred to registered eco-organizations; hazardous waste transport, if any, must be documented using bordereaux de suivi de déchets.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety inspection and record (registre de sécurité) required for premises open to the public; structural load verification by a certified technical inspector if the building receives public access; electrical installation conformity certificate issued by CONSUEL or an accredited inspection body; completion of the Dossier Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP) and occupational medical clearance for employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) — Online portal: impots.gouv.fr; Business incorporation and initial tax identification portal: formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; VAT identifiers administered by the Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL: register the company through formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr with the electronic single form (CERFA modified process); the competent company formality center transmits the file to the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE), the commercial court registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce), and the DGFiP. Upon incorporation, the company obtains a SIREN (unique company identifier), SIRET number, and is automatically registered for corporate tax. The DGFiP subsequently issues the French intra-community VAT number (numéro de TVA intracommunautaire) when the company becomes subject to VAT. For a non-resident entity without a permanent establishment, direct application to the local SIE in France is required to obtain a French VAT number and appropriate TIN. The application is made on a French VAT registration form (Cerfa 1529-sd) supported by identity documents, proof of foreign registration, and details of French commercial activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A French SARL is by default subject to French corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés, IS) as a separate tax entity. There is no general check-the-box mechanism under French law. Statutory elections include: (i) option for partnership/flow-through taxation for a family SARL under Article 239 bis AA of the French General Tax Code (CGI), available where all partners are natural persons in the same family; (ii) option for tax-consolidated group treatment (intégration fiscale) under Article 223 A CGI for groups of 95% or more controlled French entities; (iii) elections applicable under EU ATAD anti-hybrid rules where France applies provisions preventing hybrid mismatch deductions, but no elective check-the-box treatment exists. For small innovative SARLs, a reduced tax rate or loss-carry-forward eligibility may apply, but the default remains entity-level taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA) / France Value Added Tax (VAT)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general VAT registration threshold for a France-established SARL; registration is required upon any taxable economic activity, regardless of turnover. A small-business exemption ('franchise en base de TVA') applies to service providers whose annual turnover does not exceed EUR 37,500 (2025 threshold; higher threshold of EUR 85,000 for goods trading), but this exemption is a relief and does not remove the obligation to establish the company with French tax authorities; it may also require opening rights through the SIE. For non-French suppliers supplying services to French customers, immediate VAT registration is generally required without a de minimis threshold unless the EU OSS/OSS regime applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France is transitioning to compulsory electronic invoicing for domestic B2B transactions. From 1 September 2026, all companies must be able to receive e-invoices, and large enterprises must issue them electronically; from 1 September 2027, small and medium-sized enterprises (including SARLs) must issue e-invoices. E-invoicing must be transmitted through the public portal Chorus Pro or through an accredited Private Digital Platform (PDP) using the dual-flow model. E-reporting of B2C and international transactions is also mandatory. There is no continuous real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping at the national tax authority; instead, mandatory structured digital formats are transmitted on a near-real-time basis, with penalties applicable to non-compliant invoicing.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of physical goods: French VAT is chargeable at 0% under Article 262-I CGI when goods are physically delivered from France to a destination outside the EU, provided the supplier retains documentary proof that the goods left the EU within 90 days of delivery. Services supplied by a French business: B2B services supplied to a recipient outside France are generally taxable at the place of supply of the recipient (Article 259-1 B CGI), and therefore French VAT is not chargeable (effective 0% French VAT), provided the service is subject to the laws of the recipient country and the supplier obtains two independent pieces of evidence of the recipient's establishment. B2C services to non-EU customers may also fall outside French VAT if the place of supply is determined as outside France under cross-border rules (Articles 258-A and 259-D CGI). Digital design/subscription services qualify for the 'offshore services' treatment when the recipient is established outside France (EU or non-EU) and the recipient is taxable in its own jurisdiction; supporting documentation must substantiate the customer's tax ID, address, and business activity.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration d'exportation / DAE) for physical goods
Bill of Lading, Airway Bill, CMR or other transport document evidencing departure from France and arrival in a non-EU jurisdiction
Commercial invoice quoting the non-EU destination and stating the ‘Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée non applicable – Exportation hors Union Européenne’ exemption
Signed contract or purchase order with the non-EU customer and supplier delivery records
Customer confirmation receipt (Recapitulatif client / attestation de destination) for goods or services
Bank account statements and inward remittance certificate from the French bank evidencing receipt of export consideration
Intra-EU summary declaration (Échange de Biens – DEB) or sales listing (état récapitulatif) where required for intra-EU supplies
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The French tax administration (DGFiP) may apply a standard VAT assessment period of three years (extendable to six years in the case of undisclosed activity or foreign taxpayers). Fraudulent export zero-rating claims result in immediate recovery of unpaid VAT plus late payment interest (currently 0.45% per month), a 40% penalty for deliberate misstatement, and an 80% penalty for organized tax fraud or fraudulent tax maneuvers. Criminal sanctions may apply for falsifying export documents, including a fine of EUR 50,000 and imprisonment in addition to civil clawbacks. For services zero-rating, a failure to establish documentary proof outside France within a reasonable period (normally up to 180 days) exposes the exporter to VAT reassessment on the full proceeds.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France is the central bank and national authority for balance-of-payments statistics and monetary stability. The Direction Generale du Tresor (French Treasury) administers foreign-exchange policy and the foreign-investment screening regime. The Autorite de Controle Prudentiel et de Resolution (ACPR) licenses and supervises credit institutions, payment institutions and electronic money institutions under the EU CRD, PSD2 and EMD frameworks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. As an EU Member State, France applies the free movement of capital under Article 63 TFEU and does not impose general exchange controls, prior licensing for ordinary profit remittances, or registration requirements for dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders. Profit repatriation is achieved through lawful corporate distributions after statutory audit/approval and is subject to the standard 30% flat withholding tax (or a lower treaty rate under income tax treaties). The only material qualification is the Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) screening regime under Articles L151-3 et seq. and R153-9 of the French Monetary and Financial Code, which requires prior ministerial authorization for investments in sensitive sectors such as defence, cybersecurity, critical infrastructure, artificial intelligence with dual-use application, and other strategically protected activities. A UI/UX design subscription agency classified under ISIC 7410 / NAICS 541430 does not fall within that protected perimeter; therefore no prior authorization is required for non-resident capital injection. Balance-of-payments reporting obligations apply for statistical purposes only.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation timeline. Export invoices may be denominated in any currency freely agreed between the parties. The only compliance duties are: (i) balance-of-payments reporting to Banque de France via the intermediary credit institution for each cross-border transfer at or above EUR 50,000 (or monthly aggregate reporting at the same threshold); (ii) completion of the Banque de France 'green form' declaration when payments are made without bank intermediation; and (iii) a cash declaration to French customs for physical banknotes and negotiable instruments of EUR 10,000 or more transported across the border. There is no obligation to convert export proceeds into euros.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital escrow account (compte de depot de capital) and operational EUR current account with treasury and international trade desk
Capital escrow account (compte bloque) and operational EUR current account with dedicated SME and international banking solutions
Operational EUR current account post-registration; capital escrow available through branch-based deposit account
Capital escrow account and operational EUR business account
Operational EUR business account with commercial banking services; capital escrow available at branch level

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High as a complementary treasury and collections rail, but not a complete substitute for tier-1 bank accounts. Qonto (French electronic money institution licensed by ACPR), Wise Europe S.A. (Irish-authorised EMI passporting into France under PSD2) and Stripe Billing (French payment institution) can onboard the low-risk UI/UX design subscription company remotely within 24-48 hours, provide a French or European EUR IBAN, execute SEPA Credit Transfers, receive inbound SWIFT MT103 payments, and facilitate multi-currency conversions at competitive rates. Legal constraints: EMIs and payment institutions are not credit institutions; client funds are safeguarded in segregated accounts under Article L.526-1 et seq. of the French Monetary and Financial Code and are not covered by the French deposit guarantee fund (FGDR). EMIs cannot grant overdrafts, working-capital loans, trade finance, or standby letters of credit, and they are subject to restrictions on investment activities. For this entity, the optimal structure is: tier-1 bank for capital escrow, operational treasury, and credit facilities; Stripe Billing as the principal card/subscription collection rail; and Wise for cost-efficient cross-border disbursements and FX execution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French AML/KYC legislation under Article L.561-5 of the Monetary and Financial Code requires identification of the corporate client, its legal representatives (the SARL gérant), the ownership chain, and every beneficial owner holding 25% or more. Legacy tier-1 banks generally expect a physical branch visit by the gérant for signature specimen and identity verification, particularly when the SARL has non-resident shareholders or a non-resident manager; many large banks additionally require an interview (on-site or via secure video) covering the business model, source of funds, expected transaction flows, and counterparties. Since Ordonnance No. 2020-1543, remote onboarding with eIDAS-compliant digital identity verification and biometric/liveness checks is legally permitted, and some banks accept fully remote KYC where the solution meets ACPR security expectations. In practice, for a non-resident-owned SARL, most tier-1 banks still require at least one physical presence or a notarized and apostilled power of attorney in favour of a professional domiciliation agent or a French-resident signatory. Recommended mandate: schedule a formation-stage appointment at the chosen bank, bring the original passport, proof of residential address, the corporate Kbis extract (or draft statuts for pre-registration opening), the RBE beneficial-ownership filing receipt, and certified bank statements of the shareholders evidencing source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-resident shareholding structure or intermediate holding companies in low-disclosure jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial-ownership register (Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs) filed at the Greffe with receipt; full chain-of-title documentation comprising share registers, notarized corporate family tree, apostilled certificates of good standing from each intermediary jurisdiction; a UBO matrix with full name, date of birth, passport copy, and percentage of ownership; and a signed officer questionnaire disclosing source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound initial capital originating from countries on the FATF grey list, high-risk non-treaty jurisdictions, or jurisdictions with deficient AML frameworks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sworn declaration of origin of funds backed by shareholder bank statements from a regulated bank over a six-month lookback period; supporting evidence such as employment contracts, salary slips, asset-disposal deeds, inheritance documents, or notarized gift deeds; tax-residency certificates of the shareholders; and post-funding SARL Kbis and bank certificate confirming the receipt and blocking of share capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of digital-only rails, virtual IBANs, crypto exchanges, or commingled fintech accounts prior to tier-1 bank onboarding
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Itemized ledger of all Stripe and Wise payment flows since inception; downloadable MT103/SEPA statement lines; bank transaction reports; a clean-source cash-flow budget demonstrating no mingling of personal and corporate funds; and a capital-formation memorandum explaining the chronological movement of each contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Subscription-based software/design service model with high-velocity cross-border inflows presenting perceived money-laundering-through-invoicing risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Standard client subscription agreements and order forms; deliverables evidence such as design audits, Figma collaboration records, and interface specifications; invoice register with correct VAT treatment (French VAT and EU reverse-charge where applicable); Stripe merchant reporting and settlement schedules; and a written justification of the low-risk classification for ISIC 7410 design-subscription services.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For the formation of the SARL, shareholders must pay their capital contributions in euros into a blocked capital-deposit account (compte de depot de capital) held either with a French credit institution, a notary, or the Caisse des Depots et Consignations. The depositary issues the certificat de depot des fonds, which is attached to the M0 application for registration at the Registre du Commerce et des Societes (Greffe). Upon issuance of the Kbis, the blocked account is released and the capital is transferred to the SARL operational account. For a non-resident shareholder injecting funds from abroad, the compliant routing is an inbound SWIFT MT103 wire from the shareholder's regulated bank, retaining the ISO 20022 UETR reference and using the Banque de France balance-of-payments code for direct investment (capital subscription or paid-in equity); the wire narrative must identify the company name, the words 'apport en numeraire', and the reference to the blocked capital account. The receiving bank will apply standard funds-verification and, for transfers at or above EUR 50,000, the transaction will be captured in the balance-of-payments reporting to Banque de France. No prior ministerial authorization is required because the UI/UX design subscription business is not in a protected strategic sector; however, if the foreign shareholder holds sensitive corporate characteristics, the bank may request an FDI statement and additional UBO documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine trade settlements with EU beneficiaries should be executed through SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer for same-day delivery; an SWIFT MT103 is unnecessary within the SEPA zone. For non-EU counterparties such as UK, US, and Asian subcontractors, licensors, cloud providers, and design freelancers, the appropriate clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 with gpi tracking (including UETR) with the invoice reference and a purpose code consistent with cross-border services. For larger enterprise contracts above approximately EUR 300,000, a vendor may request a documentary commercial letter of credit (sight LC issued via SWIFT MT700) or a standby letter of credit (SWIFT MT760) securing the SARL's subscription or milestone-payment obligations; these instruments are available from BNP Paribas or Societe Generale against the client subscription-receivable portfolio with invoice-assignment collateral. All outbound service payments must be supported by a signed service agreement, a compliant invoice, a transfer-purpose annotation, and, where the aggregate transfers to one counterparty exceed EUR 50,000 per month, the bank will include the flows in the Banque de France balance-of-payments file. For freelancer payments in USD, GBP, or other currencies, banks execute local clearing rails in the destination currency with FX conversion at day rates, and the correct purpose code 'compensation of services' should be applied.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable forward contracts (plain-vanilla OTC FX forwards) with a licensed French credit institution, limited to underlying commercial exposure from USD-denominated subscription revenue
EUR/GBP deliverable forward contracts for UK client billings and subcontractor payments
Purchased EUR/USD FX options and zero-cost collars for protection of design-retainer revenue without asymmetric risk
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) for medium-term balance-sheet hedging if capital injections or acquisition funding are denominated in USD
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for non-convertible or thinly traded currencies hedged on an underlying commercial transaction basis
Listed EUR/USD currency futures traded on EU-regulated exchanges as an alternative when bank OTC credit lines are constrained

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts approval by the shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SARL; minutes retained in the company's records
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A court may order the manager to convene the shareholders; failure to prepare or submit accounts may result in civil or criminal sanctions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial court registry (greffe), through the French business formalities portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval, or two months for electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The president of the commercial court may order filing under a daily penalty; failure to file may incur a criminal fine, generally up to EUR 1,500 and EUR 3,000 for repeat offences. No automatic strike-off period applies.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Form 2065 and attachments)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the financial year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, generally by the second working day after 1 May, subject to the applicable electronic-filing calendar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing interest and surcharges apply; the surcharge is generally 10% absent a formal notice and may increase after notice or in cases of deliberate non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual value-added tax return, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French tax administration (Direction générale des Finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Under the company's VAT regime: annual CA12 deadline for the simplified regime or periodic CA3 deadlines for the normal regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest and statutory surcharges may apply; repeated non-compliance can lead to tax reassessment and collection measures.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) is generally required when the SARL exceeds at least two of these three thresholds at year-end: EUR 5 million total assets, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional requirements can apply to groups, controlled entities, or upon a qualifying shareholder request or court order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the Plan comptable général (PCG) for individual statutory accounts. IFRS is generally relevant to consolidated accounts of listed groups, not ordinary SARL individual accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not generally require a separate annual UBO confirmation. File an update with the competent registry when beneficial ownership information changes, generally within 30 days. Record share transfers and resulting changes in the company's corporate documentation and make any required amendment to the articles or registry filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Shareholders' decisions and meeting minutes, maintained in the legally required form
Share-transfer records and supporting instruments, as applicable
Beneficial ownership information and filed declarations, as applicable

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: EUR 300–1,500 annually for a commercial domiciliation service; no separate fee where the company uses its own premises
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: EUR 2,000–6,000 annually for a small company subject to statutory audit; scope and complexity may increase fees

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 25% headline rate with R&D tax credits (up to 30% of eligible expenses), accelerated depreciation allowances, and temporary tax holidays in designated zones or for innovative activities

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1200 - Déclaration des résultats via e-impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 3 months after fiscal year-end (e.g., 31 March for calendar year ending 31 December)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from all commercial activities including design services and subscription fees
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents must file through a French tax representative or proxy; report all taxable income

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit before corporate tax after deducting all allowable expenses, provisions, and amortizations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for transfer pricing adjustments if applicable; non-residents limited to French-sourced income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: 0.5% of tax due per month of delay (minimum €50, maximum 25% of tax due); plus interest on late payments and potential criminal sanctions

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 12.8% flat tax (PFU) on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit TRC (Traitement de la demande de relief) application to French tax authorities with supporting documents such as tax residency certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and DTA articles; approval may reduce or eliminate WHT
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under most DTAs; Interest: 25% statutory rate, reduced to 0-10% under DTAs (lower for related party loans)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: 50,000,000 EUR (annual turnover threshold triggering mandatory Local File and Master File documentation)
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France enforces Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for entities in IP holding, finance, leasing, and certain high-risk activities; design and UX services generally require demonstration of real economic activity and qualified employees in France

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable income or overstatement of deductible expenses
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty: up to 5 years imprisonment and fine up to 500% of evaded tax amount
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil; directors face personal criminal liability, imprisonment, and joint restitution of taxes

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a French entity with no real business activity, employees, or decision-making in France
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative dissolution, back payment of taxes, fines up to €75,000 per infraction, and potential criminal sanctions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for fraudulent management; possible imprisonment for abuse of corporate personality

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain or provide adequate TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties up to €75,000 per year of non-compliance; potential tax reassessment and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for management errors leading to tax losses

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct proper customer due diligence or report suspicious transactions in subscription services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 5% of annual turnover; license suspension
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and potential criminal liability for complicity in money laundering
